name: Euthyroid Graves Orbitopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Euthyroid Graves Orbitopathy

criteria.description: Presence of orbital inflammation signs such as eyelid edema, conjunctival injection, or chemosis
Normal thyroid function tests (euthyroid state) without clinical or biochemical hyper- or hypothyroidism
Orbital imaging (CT or MRI) showing extraocular muscle enlargement without other orbital pathology
Presence of thyroid autoantibodies (e.g., TSH receptor antibodies) supportive but not mandatory
Exclusion of other causes of orbital inflammation or proptosis such as orbital tumors or infections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of orbital inflammation signs, normal thyroid function tests, characteristic orbital imaging findings, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging and laboratory tests; thyroid autoantibodies may be absent or low titer.

laboratory: Normal thyroid hormone levels (TSH, free T4, free T3)
Variable presence of TSH receptor antibodies or thyroid peroxidase antibodies
imaging: Orbital CT or MRI showing enlargement of extraocular muscles sparing tendinous insertions
Absence of orbital masses or abscess
other: Clinical exclusion of other orbital inflammatory or neoplastic conditions

distinguishingFeatures: More frequent and severe systemic thyroid dysfunction
Acute onset with severe orbital pain
Diffuse orbital inflammation including tendinous insertions on imaging

redFlags: Sudden vision loss or severe visual acuity decrease
Signs of optic neuropathy (color vision defects, afferent pupillary defect)
Severe orbital pain with fever suggesting infection
